sourceEvidence.label: D13-D23 memory and request-capacity findings plus inspected source

assessment.summary: Controlled retrieval from existing bounded tool results is a first design candidate; added long-term result capture needs separate evidence and data policy.

nonNegotiables: Prioritize test and MCP results over historical file-content snapshots.
MCP retrieval candidates must originate from allowlisted services and tools.
Sensitive logs must not be sent to the model service on first tool return or historical retrieval.
Retrieval must not expand sensitive-content visibility or grant external-send authority.
assumptions: No measured storage, latency or retention budget was supplied.
Concurrent source edits must be rechecked before implementation.

opportunities.title: Bounded historical tool-result retrieval
opportunities.summary: Give the model scoped access to safe projections of prior test and MCP results without treating history as authority.
opportunities.diagnosis: Durable results exist, but there is no model-facing scoped retrieval path or complete request-capacity check; redaction alone cannot certify safe visibility.

evidence.claim: Request budget does not account for the complete final request.
The capacity gap has a separate detailed record.
The ledger persists a redacted result string in versioned JSON events; recovery/redaction.py covers named patterns rather than all sensitive values.
Tool handlers may crop model-facing output; finalization.py does not include stdout or stderr in the final evidence document.
The Docker runner disables network and mounts the whole repository read-only; runtime/assembly.py may select this or a trusted host runner.
Current history projection cannot reconstruct full tool-result bodies for the model.

desiredInvariants: Every result reference is bound to a caller, thread, workspace, tool call and persisted version.
Test and MCP free-text output must pass a model-ingress gate before the first tool result and every historical replay; unknown or sensitive logs yield metadata only.
Unknown sensitivity yields metadata only; retrieved text conveys no approval authority.
All retrieved text and tool definitions count toward a pre-send full-request budget.
Each response states capture, retention and read truncation separately.

options.title: Index safe metadata from existing events
options.summary: Gate first-return tool output, then build a rebuildable metadata index over old events without releasing old result bodies.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A complete final request check is still required.
Retrieval quotas cannot replace total request accounting.
Scoped reads narrow new exposure; existing stored sensitive data remains a separate concern.
Already cropped content cannot be recreated.
Search over existing results does not prove secret-free test execution; a separate safe execution boundary is required for rich output.

tradeoffs.assessment: A model-ingress gate protects both initial tool return and scoped historical reads; old persisted content may still be sensitive.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test secret-bearing first returns, cross-thread denial and unknown-sensitivity metadata-only behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Index and read queries add local database work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p95 retrieval latency on representative long threads.

tradeoffs.assessment: A bounded index and page buffers use memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak process memory and index size.

tradeoffs.assessment: Historical failures may become diagnosable, provided the needed text survived cropping.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare task recovery and retry counts using the same scenarios.

tradeoffs.assessment: Search denial, stale references and index rebuilding need observable status.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise index corruption and recovery diagnostics.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing result events need no body migration; derived indexes can be rebuilt.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Build and remove the index against a copy of an old database.

residualRisks: Existing result bodies may contain sensitive text missed by regex redaction.
Old metadata alone may not support diagnosis.

workPackages: Build rebuildable short index and paged reader
acceptanceCriteria: Secret-bearing logs do not enter model requests
Retrieved content cannot bypass request capacity
migrationNotes: Existing events are not automatically low sensitivity
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable search and read endpoints and discard the derived index; preserve the model-ingress gate.

options.title: Persist the model-safe first-return projection
options.summary: Generate a bounded model-safe projection before the first tool return and persist that exact projection for later scoped retrieval.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The final request capacity check remains mandatory.
Longer storage does not change provider context limits.
Pre-storage classification is needed beyond pattern redaction.
Allowed diagnostics survive as the first-return projection, but never executor capture truncation.
Longer capture still needs a separate safe execution boundary before rich output can reach the model.

tradeoffs.assessment: The same model-ingress decision governs first return and retrieval; a projection mistake can persist sensitive data.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Adversarial tests for secrets and private data in first-return and historical test/MCP output.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional serialization and writes increase tool completion latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark tool completion p95 on large outputs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Longer bounded buffers and indexes require more resources.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak memory and database growth per long task.

tradeoffs.assessment: Better diagnostics compete with new write and cleanup failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject write, replay and cleanup failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Classification, retention deadlines and cleanup require monitoring and incident procedures.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review rejection telemetry and rehearse expired-data cleanup.

tradeoffs.assessment: New event types and durable data policies require compatibility and rollback decisions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Upgrade and roll back a copied old database.

residualRisks: Content discarded by executor capture limits remains unavailable.
An unsafe first-return projection can persist sensitive material.

workPackages: Define model-safe projection and policy version
Persist the first-return projection as a typed event
Add scoped index, reader and budget gate
acceptanceCriteria: Historical reads reveal no more than first return
Read responses expose all truncation states
migrationNotes: Old events are not retroactively promoted to low sensitivity
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop new projection persistence and reads; preserve first-return model-ingress checks.

opportunities.recommendation: Expose only metadata from old events; for new results persist the exact model-safe first-return projection and retrieve that projection under current scope and budget checks.

openQuestions: Which test and MCP outputs are safe to expose beyond metadata?
What deterministic structured diagnostics let the model repair failures without reading free-text logs?
Can any test profiles be proven to run only on synthetic model-shareable inputs with no access to credentials, sensitive files or network?
Would a separately constructed allowlisted workspace be required for model-shareable test output?
Who owns test-profile output contracts, and what runtime control permits each structured failure field to reach the model?
What retention duration and per-thread storage quota should apply?
How will content-level egress policy consume data labels from retrieval?
